* **Hindustan Times** (June 07 2024): The article states that claims of PM Modi offering free recharge schemes have gone viral multiple times, and the Press Information Bureau (PIB) has clarified that neither the Indian Government nor PM Modi is running any such scheme. It warns against clicking on suspicious links as they may lead to data theft and scams. [1]
* **Telugu Post** (October 29 2023): This source reports on a viral WhatsApp message claiming the BJP is providing three months of free recharge to all Indian mobile service customers. It debunks the claim, stating that no such announcement has been made by the BJP or the central government, and the linked website is not official. [2]
* **The Quint** (December 29 2023): The Quint fact-checked a fake post claiming PM Modi was offering free Rs 239 recharge to voters ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha Elections. They found no evidence of such an announcement and warned that the linked website collects user data and could lead to financial scams. [3]
* **LatestLY** (September 04 2026): This article reports that PIB Fact Check has debunked a viral message claiming PM Narendra Modi is offering three months of free mobile recharge. The government confirmed that no such scheme exists and warned citizens against fraudulent links. [4]
* **PIB Fact Check (Facebook)** (August 05 2026): A Facebook post from PIB Fact Check clarifies that a digitally altered video claiming PM Narendra Modi is offering 3 months of free mobile recharge to all students is fake. It states that no such announcement has been made by the Prime Minister. [5] [6]
* **Prabhat Khabar** (September 07 2026): This source reiterates that PIB Fact Check has clarified that no such scheme for free mobile recharge is being run by the Prime Minister or the central government. It advises people to be vigilant and not forward such messages. [7]
